scope: Dated research snapshot of selected current text/code families, not exhaustive availability or immutable served-model proof.
policy_notes: This establishes temporal separation from provider-documented cutoffs, not proof that a model never encountered a CVE through later training, provider context, retrieval, or evaluation contamination.
Use training-data cutoff rather than earlier reliable-knowledge cutoff for conservative CVE filtering.
Release dates and model-ID snapshot dates must not be substituted for training-data cutoff.
Z.ai has no published temporal knowledge cutoff in the official model guides/cards/repository/report reviewed, including required GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3.
Other current xAI families lack verified opened-source cutoffs; Grok 4.6 historical candidate appears only in stale search-index excerpts.
Versioned API IDs are not exact immutable weight hashes. Provider alias routing can change and must be logged with endpoint and execution date.
A published knowledge cutoff alone is not proof that later post-training excluded a particular CVE.

routing_notes: GLM Coding Plan routes GLM-5.2/5.1 to GLM-5.3, GLM-4.7 to GLM-5.3-Flash; standard API docs still list original IDs, so endpoint distinction is mandatory.
xAI May 15 retirement redirects grok-4-1-fast-reasoning, grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, grok-4-fast-reasoning, grok-4-fast-non-reasoning, grok-4-0709 and grok-3 to grok-4.3.

The retirement page's prose broadly includes grok-code-fast-1 in the grok-4.3 redirect, but its table and current Grok Build model page identify grok-build-0.1. Use current model detail as stronger specific evidence and retain this documentation inconsistency.

mode_notes.note: GPT-5.6 pro mode keeps selected model ID and sets reasoning.mode=pro. Do not invent a separate OpenAI -pro ID.
GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 support standard/pro execution modes; API example uses gpt-6.1-sol with reasoning.mode=pro.
For a -latest alias, inspect the returned model because alias resolution can change and depends on approved access.
